participating-org.narrative: Billital Maroobé is a regional pastoralist network of Sahelian organisations of cattle herders and breeders. The network was created by three pastoralist organisations in 2003. Each of them had a national base: Tassagh in Mali, CRUS in Burkina Faso and AREN in Niger. Recently, other pastoralist alliances have joint Billital Maroobé, so that the intervention zone expanded with four new countries: Mauretania, Senegal, Benin and Nigeria. The present seven member organisations (apart from the three founding organisations ADENA, Miyetti Allah, Udoper and FNEM) will build national alliances to increase their base and legitimacy. Billital Maroobé is convinced that the pastoralist way of living is sustainable and economically feasible if some conditions changed: a enabling a legal framework in favour of (international) transhumance, infrastructures in favour of the marketing of cattle, an improved access to essential services and a equitable representation of pastoralists in political and administrative bodies.
